What we’re saying is Australia has to have the capacity to bring in an Australian culture, a culture with guardrails, a culture that is able to absorb people so that we have harmony, we have peace, and we have a unity of purpose. If you get a Balkanisation in Australia where there are so many people in so many different corners that they basically live their culture not an Australian culture, then inherently that just does not work out. Qantas plans to launch a nonstop service between Sydney and either London Heathrow or New York JFK by late 2027 – five years later than originally scheduled. London has always been the flagship destination for the Australian airline. Even if the US city is chosen first, the Heathrow link will follow close behind and will be by far the longest passenger flight in the world in terms of direct distance. Currently the title holder is Singapore Airlines from its hub to New York JFK at 9,537 miles. The London-Sydney distance is over 1,000 miles further, at 10,573 miles – nearly two hours' extra flying.

Connecting New South Wales with the UK is much more of a challenge than Western Australia. The direct distance from Sydney and London is one-sixth more than from Perth, beyond the range of any currently available passenger aircraft when fully loaded. While Qantas test flights with a small number of passengers on board have made the London-Sydney trip nonstop (as early as 1989), the trick is to find an aircraft that can successfully operate between the two cities with a full payload of passengers and cargo. The task is made more difficult by the current closure of Russian airspace to "western" carriers including British Airways, Singapore Airlines and Qantas. The airline has ordered a dozen specially configured Airbus A350-1000 aircraft, each fitted with an additional 20,000 litre fuel tank, enabling them to fly for 22 hours without refuelling.

Qantas plans to launch a nonstop service between Sydney and either London Heathrow or New York JFK by late 2027 – five years later than originally scheduled.

London has always been the flagship destination for the Australian airline. Even if the US city is chosen first, the Heathrow link will follow close behind and will be by far the longest passenger flight in the world in terms of direct distance.

Currently the title holder is Singapore Airlines from its hub to New York JFK at 9,537 miles. The London-Sydney distance is over 1,000 miles further, at 10,573 miles – nearly two hours' extra flying.

Qantas says the new nonstop link will overcome "the tyranny of distance". But will people really want to step on board for a gruelling journey of up to 20 hours? And what about the adverse environmental effects?

These are the key questions and answers.

The Australian carrier flies nonstop between London and Perth, a direct distance of 9,009 miles. The route was launched in March 2018 and, with the exception of the Covid pandemic, has proved extremely popular. However, due to the extended flight time caused by avoiding Middle East conflict zones, Russian and Ukrainian airspace, the westbound Perth-London service is refuelling en route in Singapore at least until 25 July 2026. The prevailing jet stream means journeys in this direction take longer.

Connecting New South Wales with the UK is much more of a challenge than Western Australia. The direct distance from Sydney and London is one-sixth more than from Perth, beyond the range of any currently available passenger aircraft when fully loaded.

While Qantas test flights with a small number of passengers on board have made the London-Sydney trip nonstop (as early as 1989), the trick is to find an aircraft that can successfully operate between the two cities with a full payload of passengers and cargo.

The task is made more difficult by the current closure of Russian airspace to "western" carriers including British Airways, Singapore Airlines and Qantas.

The airline has ordered a dozen specially configured Airbus A350-1000 aircraft, each fitted with an additional 20,000 litre fuel tank, enabling them to fly for 22 hours without refuelling.

payload.title: Qantasin suorat Sydney–Lontoo-lennot lykkääntyvät jälleen
payload.summary: Qantas arvioi nyt, että Project Sunrise -hankkeen ensimmäinen lento toteutuu marraskuussa 2027. Samassa Australian uutispäivässä Etelä-Australiassa torjuttiin aborttilakia koskenut esitys, jota maan keskeiset terveysalan järjestöt vastustivat.
payload.content:
Qantas on siirtänyt jälleen aikatauluaan pitkään valmistelluille suorille lennoille Sydneystä Lontooseen ja mahdollisesti New Yorkiin. Yhtiö arvioi nyt, että Project Sunrise -hankkeen ensimmäinen lento lähtisi marraskuussa 2027. Australiassa päivän uutisiin kuului myös Etelä-Australian aborttilakiesityksen kaatuminen terveysalan järjestöjen vastustuksen jälkeen.

## Maailman pisimmäksi kaavailtu reitti

Qantasin suunnitelmana on avata suora yhteys Sydneystä joko Lontoon Heathrow’n lentoasemalle tai New Yorkin JFK:lle vuoden 2027 loppuun mennessä. Aikataulu on noin viisi vuotta alkuperäistä suunnitelmaa myöhempi.

Lontoo on ollut hankkeen keskeinen kohde, vaikka New York voisi lähteiden mukaan tulla valituksi ensimmäiseksi reitiksi. Jos näin tapahtuu, Heathrow’n-yhteyden arvioidaan seuraavan pian perässä. Sydney–Lontoo olisi suoran etäisyyden perusteella maailman pisin matkustajalentoreitti.

Nykyinen pisin reitti on Singapore Airlinesin lento Singaporesta New Yorkiin, jonka pituus on 9 537 mailia. Lontoon ja Sydneyn välinen etäisyys on 10 573 mailia eli yli tuhat mailia pidempi. Se tarkoittaisi lähes kahta tuntia lisää lentoaikaa.

## Tekniset vaatimukset ovat poikkeukselliset

Sydney–Lontoo-yhteys on Qantasille vaikeampi kuin Länsi-Australiasta lähtevät suorat lennot. Etäisyys New South Walesista Britanniaan on noin kuudesosan pidempi kuin Perthistä Lontooseen, ja täyteen lastatun matkustajakoneen toimintamatka on ollut keskeinen rajoite.

Qantas on tehnyt suoria koelentoja Lontoon ja Sydneyn välillä pienellä matkustajamäärällä jo vuonna 1989. Varsinainen haaste on kuitenkin liikennöidä reittiä täydessä matkustaja- ja rahtikäytössä. Tilannetta vaikeuttaa myös Venäjän ilmatilan sulku länsimaisilta lentoyhtiöiltä, kuten British Airwaysilta, Singapore Airlinesilta ja Qantasilta.

Yhtiö on tilannut kaksitoista erikoisvarusteltua Airbus A350-1000 -konetta. Niihin asennetaan ylimääräinen 20 000 litran polttoainesäiliö, jonka on määrä mahdollistaa jopa 22 tunnin lennot ilman välilaskua.

## Aborttilakiesitys torjuttiin Etelä-Australiassa

Etelä-Australiassa aborttilakia koskenut esitys ei edennyt. Sitä vastustivat keskeiset lääketieteelliset järjestöt, kuten Australian ja Uuden-Seelannin synnytys- ja naistentautilääkärien kollegio, Australian Medical Association sekä kätilöiden järjestö.

Lähdetietojen mukaan yli 90 prosenttia aborteista tehdään ensimmäisen raskauskolmanneksen aikana. Etelä-Australian terveysviranomaisten vuoden 2023 tietojen mukaan alle yksi prosentti aborteista, 47 tapausta, tehtiin myöhemmässä vaiheessa.

Sydney–Lontoo-reitistä tulisi suoran etäisyyden perusteella maailman pisin matkustajalentoreitti.
Etelä-Australiassa aborttilakiesitys kaatui terveysalan keskeisten järjestöjen vastustuksen jälkeen.

Qantas plans to launch a nonstop service between Sydney and either London Heathrow or New York JFK by late 2027 – five years later than originally scheduled. London has always been the flagship destination for the Australian airline. Even if the US city is chosen first, the Heathrow link will follow close behind and will be by far the longest passenger flight in the world in terms of direct distance. Currently the title holder is Singapore Airlines from its hub to New York JFK at 9,537 miles. The London-Sydney distance is over 1,000 miles further, at 10,573 miles – nearly two hours' extra flying.

Connecting New South Wales with the UK is much more of a challenge than Western Australia. The direct distance from Sydney and London is one-sixth more than from Perth, beyond the range of any currently available passenger aircraft when fully loaded. While Qantas test flights with a small number of passengers on board have made the London-Sydney trip nonstop (as early as 1989), the trick is to find an aircraft that can successfully operate between the two cities with a full payload of passengers and cargo. The task is made more difficult by the current closure of Russian airspace to "western" carriers including British Airways, Singapore Airlines and Qantas. The airline has ordered a dozen specially configured Airbus A350-1000 aircraft, each fitted with an additional 20,000 litre fuel tank, enabling them to fly for 22 hours without refuelling.
